_comment: The ledger and the rooms that open. The ledger is the order's work book - the open half of the Good Cheer Club roll, listing the jobs not done yet, the trade each one carries, and a blank line for the name of whoever does it. The rooms are the home side of those jobs: sealed, visibly unfinished parts of the hall that open for good when a keeper's crates have paid for them. Design in docs/QUESTS.md; the five rungs are Chris's, 2026-10-26.
_values: The four crate costs below are CHRIS'S, kept on review on 2026-10-27 - 'Keep the 1/3/6/10 room costs for now.' They started as Claude's proposal on 2026-10-26 and are no longer that. 1 / 3 / 6 / 10 is a first-session door and then a widening gap. 'For now' is his word and it means these are a playtest away from moving, so change them when the sessions say to - nothing in the code assumes an ordering or a spacing. What is settled is that they are a deliberate choice rather than a placeholder nobody has read.
_crateRule: A room costs crates that are COMMITTED, not deducted. profile.contributions.RestorationCrates is a credited total and the handoff locked it as never removable - you cannot take your name off the roll. So spending is derived: available = that total minus the cost of every room already opened. The gross figure the three landmark plates read is untouched by opening a room, which is correct, because the landmarks record what you brought home and the rooms record what you did with it.
_whoseHall: The hall in the world is the host keeper's, per docs/DECISIONS.md O5. Only the host's rooms are shown and only the host can open one; a visitor reads the hall and their own figure, exactly as the landmark plates already behave. Visiting a friend's Lanternhold to see what they have rebuilt is the point of it.

rooms.sealed: Boarded over. The departure board runs off whatever is in here.
rooms.restored: The generator turns over. The board lights.

rooms.sealed: A bench under a sheet, and no tools on the wall.
rooms.restored: The bench is clear and the wall is hung.

rooms.sealed: The gate is down. Nothing has moved in this shaft for a long time.
rooms.restored: The gate rises. The hall has two floors again.

rooms.sealed: A desk, an aerial lead, and no set on the desk.
rooms.restored: The set warms up. Somebody, somewhere, is still transmitting.

rungs.title: RESTORE THE DEPARTURE GENERATOR
rungs.job: Salvage fuses and wiring from the ground floor.
rungs.opens: Reliable departures, and markers on the board.
rungs.wakes: Powered lights. The Window Walkers stand up.

restoration._comment: The mechanical half of rung one, and the only rung that has one yet. Chris's four prose fields above are untouched; this says what they mean in code. Shape: a room that must be open, salvage that is spent, a thing that changes, a thing that wakes. A later rung adds a block like this one and needs no new system.
restoration._values: EVERY NUMBER IN THIS BLOCK IS PROPOSED, by Claude, not chosen by Chris. Written as real values rather than zeroes so the rung can be played and felt. 4 Components is roughly one careful ground-floor sweep; the false start is the whole reason 'reliable' is a reward.
restoration._requiresRoomNote: Both halves of the same job: the crates open the room at home, the salvage makes the generator in it turn over. The room's own 'restored' line - 'The generator turns over. The board lights.' - is this event, which is why the room and the rung were already linked.
restoration._salvageNote: Chris's job line is 'salvage fuses and wiring from the ground floor'. Fuses and wiring are Components in data/loot.json. Spent, not credited: unlike crates, which the handoff locked as never removable from a keeper's roll, these leave the stash. WorkshopService already spends materials this way.
restoration._wakesNote: Powered light is light the keepers do not carry, so going dark stops protecting them from anything that wakes to light. Named explicitly rather than applied to every light-waking enemy, because Chris said the Window Walkers stand up and said nothing about the ficus, which wakes the same way and is approved but undefined.
restoration._departureNote: What 'reliable departures' is a reward FOR. Before the generator the board runs on whatever is left in the room: a twelve-second wind-up that fails better than a third of the time and sends the crew back to the board. After it, five seconds, every time. The board states this before a keeper presses it - a trade you find out about afterwards is not a trade.

rungs.title: RECOVER THE WORKSHOP TOOLS
rungs.opens: A defensive tool, and a noisemaker.
rungs.wakes: The staff corridors. Sweepers patrol them.

rungs.title: BRING BACK THE LIFT PARTS
rungs.job: Heavy salvage, out of the stockrooms.

rungs.title: RESTORE THE LANTERNHOLD RADIO
rungs.opens: Warnings, leads, and better word on the way out.
rungs.wakes: Glimmers. And it broadcasts the crew.

rungs.title: OPEN THE LOADING DOCK GATE
rungs.job: More than one trip. The gate is seized.
rungs.opens: The next section of the mall.
rungs.wakes: A straighter road in, for the Warden.
rungs._noRoom: The only rung with no room at home: its whole reward is out there. Deliberate - see docs/QUESTS.md.

_rungState: Rung one is built end to end as of 2026-10-27 (docs/WORKLIST.md A9): it has a `restoration` block above, RestorationService owns the flag and the cost, and the ledger board prints it as DONE once a keeper has done it. The other four rungs are still read-only text and print as not begun with their trade stated. Each one becomes real by gaining a `restoration` block - there is no quest state machine to extend, which was the point of doing the first one small.
_restorationRule: A restoration is one flag per keeper, persisted on their profile beside `rooms`, and it never reverses. It is not a run-scoped buff and it is not purchasable: the only way to set it is to open the room and spend the salvage. Values here are proposed; the shape is not. See docs/QUESTS.md for why no restoration is reversible and why nothing on the ladder ever makes light free.
